topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, intrinsic mutation, and environmental risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental drivers of cancer development, examining the interplay between intrinsic genetic mutations, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological agents, including viruses and bacteria, contribute to oncogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical carcinogenesis and tumor promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical agents, chemical mutagens, metabolic activation, and promotional microenvironments drive DNA damage and tumor progression.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and assessing cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe experimental, genomic, and epidemiological approaches used to detect carcinogenicity and evaluate carcinogenic risk in human populations.

topics.label: Conclusion and final takeaways
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks and final summary of the lecture.
